issues.body: Section 5 says every secret must live in `dispatch-secrets` and that there must be no second secret-bearing environment, but section 6 concedes that the guard neither enumerates other environments nor fails if they contain secrets. As the document itself explains, a secret in another environment can then be exposed by a consumer bound to that environment at an attacker-controlled ref without the verified branch policy. This is the same default-allow class the strategy claims to eliminate, so recording it as a follow-up is insufficient for a complete pre-cutover trust strategy.
issues.fix_hint: Make the cutover contingent on a guard that paginates the repository environment listing, fails closed on any unreadable/incomplete response, enumerates secrets for every environment, and rejects secret-bearing environments other than `dispatch-secrets`; add non-vacuous self-tests for an alternate environment containing a secret and for failed/truncated pagination. Alternatively, narrow this document so it does not establish or rely on the unenforced invariant and explicitly state that #266 remains blocked until that guard lands.
issues.title: The chosen strategy leaves its single-environment invariant unenforced

verdict.summary: The shared `dispatch-secrets` choice is reasoned clearly, and the document accurately calls out its loss of per-job least privilege. However, the proposed repo-wide strategy is not complete or fail-closed: it establishes “no second secret-bearing environment” as a security rule while explicitly acknowledging that no guard verifies that rule. That leaves an unprotected alternate environment as a default-allow secret-exfiltration path. A trust-plane strategy should not authorize the value cutover while its own stated invariant is merely advisory.
